messages:
Ana: Heads up — saw a weird spike in p95 on the latency dashboard for /v1/generate in eu-west after yesterday's routing weight change. p50 looks fine but p95 and p99 disagree with raw histogram.
Kevin: Can you paste the dashboard slice and the route weights you changed?
Ana: Quick grab: route weights moved: default 0.7 -> 0.5, fallback-route 0.3 -> 0.5. Dashboard query: `service=frontend endpoint=/v1/generate | percentile(50,95,99)` (console panel).
Maria: Did the quota fallback change too? If some clients hit quota and fall through we may be blending two latency populations. That could alias percentiles.
Joel: Also check sample counts. When tdigest merges sparse and dense groups you can get weird jumps if one subgroup has very few samples but extreme values.
Ana: Sample counts on that slice: p50 count 1200, p95 sample_count ~ 18, p99 sample_count ~ 6. Histogram shows a tiny tail of 2-3 requests at ~3.2s.
Kevin: That smells like a tdigest aggregation artifact. If p95/p99 derive from merged sketches and the UI aggregates by route, mixing counts with large differences can flip percentiles.
console-team: Confirmed — console currently uses route-level t-digests and then does a merge for the panel. We added a fast-merge path last release; it assumes reasonably uniform sample counts.
sre-bot: alert: route-weight-change-triggered >10% p95 delta on /v1/generate (detected 2024-11-03T07:12Z)
Maria: Two possible causes: real tail due to fallback route being slower, or merge aliasing. Quick check: what are p95s per route before merge?
Ana: Per-route raw percentiles: default-route p95=0.18s, fallback-route p95=3.1s. So yes, fallback-route has a heavy tail but very low volume. After increasing its weight, merged p95 jumps disproportionately because the merge math pulls the high tail into the global tdigest.
Joel: Yep. If fallback had few samples previously it didn't move global p95 much; with weight increase it crosses the merge threshold. Also quota gating could amplify because some clients get throttled into fallback which are high-latency clients.
Kevin: Short-term mitigation: change UI to show provenance badges and per-route p95 alongside merged p95. Also add a sample-count threshold so we render merged percentiles only when total effective samples > N.
console-team: Agreed. We already have a sample-count badge, but it's not prominent. Proposal: (1) show per-route p95 columns, (2) add tooltip: "merged p95 may be skewed when any contributor has <50 samples" and (3) fall back to median+iqr when merged sample_count < 100.
Maria: For longer term, we should: (a) annotate the percentiles with contributor weights, (b) surface routing/quota changes in the same panel as an overlay, and (c) consider storing raw histograms for recent high-cardinality endpoints for exact recompute.
Ana: I can reproduce the spike by replaying ~200 requests with 10% routed to fallback — reproduces merged p95 jump.
Joel: Filing an infra ticket to add a tdigest merge diagnostic flag (prints contributor counts and centroids when p95 jumps >20%).
Kevin: Add a quick alert rule to suppress "merged p95" alerts when sample_count < 50 and instead alert on per-route p95 increase.
console-team: We'll sketch a UI mock: per-route pctl + merged pctl with provenance pill + sample_count threshold text. Putting a PR in for the tooltip tonight.
Ana: Thanks — creating issue and tagging @console-team @sre for follow-up. Action items: Ana to open issue, Joel to add diagnostic flag, console-team to mock UI, Kevin to adjust alerting. :white_check_mark:
Kevin: Thanks all. Quick note — when documenting, add a short explanation of tdigest merge pitfalls for oncall runbook.
Ana: Will do.
